author: greystroke
content:
Any thoughts to implementing a new issuance curve that instead of reaching 0% issuance at an arbitrary percentage of total staked ETH, to instead take the current issuance curve, and at some arbitrary percent staked, to freeze the issuance rate? Meaning above that percent stake, any additional ETH staked does not increase issuance, instead it's just even distributed among all stakers. 

If we want to try and further disincentivize new stake (at the cost of additional complexity), we could add a maturity weighting factor, where newly staked ETH gets, say, only 80% of their allotment, which slowly increases to 100% after a year or some other time period. 

It seems like a less drastic change to the issuance curve than eip-8363 which might be more palpable to the community while still moving things in the right direction. It also avoids overly aggressively reducing issuance, so we are not in a situation where we may need to reverse course in the future due to the security of the chain being undermined or insufficient issuance available to incentivize ZK provers.
